text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AD DUSTOUR
- Minister of Justice Dughmi says curtain has fallen on case of August bread rioters; all charges dropped.
- King Hussein returns to Jordan from London on Thursday; will travel on Saturday to United Arab Emirates for talks with UAE leader Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan.
- Iraqi Foreign Minister Sahhaf to visit Jordan on Friday for talks with officials.
- EU representative to Jordan says association agreement with Jordan will be signed at beginning of next year.
- Supply Minister Sobar says Jordan well stocked with food for holy month of Ramadan, has 2,000 tonnes of frozen chicken if any local shortages arise.

- Labour Minister Shakhanbeh meets representatives of spinning and weaving union, health services, general services, financial institutions and electricians who threatened to pull out of federation of labour unions because of lack of consultation.
- Ministry of Trade and Industry responds to calls for cancellation of Israeli trade fair saying it is not up to ministry to grant or refuse permission.
AL-RAI

- Finance Minister Awad says 1997 budget aims at self-sufficiency, controlling spending, conserving public funds and moving towards investment. Aims for 6.5 GDP growth in 1997, raising exports, cutting imports and controlling price rises.
- Prime Minister Kabariti, visiting free trade zone, says Jordan aims to free economy to attract investment and build up reserves.
- Trade Minister Abu al-Ragheb says Jordan wins new customs concessions in talks with Israel. Stresses links between economy and Middle East peace process.
- Source at Ministry of Water says Israel still dragging its feet over giving Jordan information needed to build dams envisaged in 1994 peace treaty.
AL-ASWAQ
- Prince Hassan says Iraq going through major transition phase.
- Labour Minister Shakhanbeh says Jordan's foreign workers number 350,000 -- but it needs only 100,000.
JORDAN TIMES
- Awad tells parliament economy in better shape than last year.
- Kabariti, visiting Zerqa free trade zones, says government plans to open similar areas in other governorates close to Jordan's borders.
